plain_explanation: Alperin's weight conjecture (blockwise numerical form) is proven for every finite group and prime. It counts the "modular" representations of a block by purely local data, and is a central conjecture in group representation theory.

subject: Algebra
title: Donovan's conjecture over fields and complete mixed-characteristic DVRs
plain_explanation: Donovan's conjecture: for blocks of finite groups with bounded defect group, there are only finitely many types up to Morita equivalence. Proven over algebraically closed fields and over Witt-vector rings.

subject: Algebra
title: Tensor saturation for even spin groups
plain_explanation: This proves tensor-product "saturation" (factor one) for the even spin groups Spin(2n), the type-D case of the simply-laced saturation conjecture.

subject: Algebra
title: Saxl’s conjecture and universal tensor squares
plain_explanation: Saxl's conjecture: the tensor square of the "staircase" representation of the symmetric group contains every irreducible representation. Proven; almost every S_n has such a universal representation.

subject: Algebra
title: Finite lattice representation and undecidability
plain_explanation: Some finite lattices are not the congruence lattice of any finite algebra, answering the Pálfy–Pudlák finite lattice representation problem negatively. Moreover, no algorithm can decide which ones are.

subject: Algebra
title: The ℓ¹-Bass conjecture for all discrete groups
plain_explanation: This proves the ℓ¹-Bass conjecture for every discrete group, and Kaplansky's idempotent conjecture over characteristic-zero domains for torsion-free groups.

subject: Algebra
title: Finite symmetric tensor categories and the Verlinde tower
plain_explanation: Every finite symmetric tensor category in characteristic p maps faithfully to a higher Verlinde category, the finite case of the Benson–Etingof–Ostrik conjecture.

subject: Algebra
title: Integral counterexamples to Gersten’s conjecture
plain_explanation: Gersten's conjecture, an injectivity statement in algebraic K-theory, is disproved integrally by explicit two-dimensional ramified regular local rings.

subject: Algebra
title: Foulkes' conjecture for sixth powers and quadratic stabilization
plain_explanation: Foulkes' conjecture compares two ways of nesting symmetric powers. This proves the sixth case, and shows a canonical map becomes surjective once b ≥ a(a − 1).

subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: The geometric phase diagram, diffusion, and spectra of random planar maps
plain_explanation: Random planar maps are random surfaces made by gluing polygons together. With Fortuin–Kasteleyn weights, this proves they converge to "Liouville quantum gravity" spheres when q ≤ 4 and collapse to a random tree when q > 4, and that random walks on them converge to Liouville Brownian motion.

subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: Planar first-passage geometry and the absence of bigeodesics
plain_explanation: First-passage percolation gives each edge of a grid a random travel time and studies the fastest routes. This proves no two-way infinite fastest route ("bigeodesic") exists in the plane, and that for exponential times the large-scale "ball" shape is strictly convex and smooth.

subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: Critical percolation on every quasi-transitive graph
plain_explanation: Percolation: keep each edge of a lattice independently with probability p. Exactly at the critical p, is there an infinite connected cluster? This proves no, on the 3D cubic lattice (a famous open problem) and on every quasi-transitive graph.

subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: The Benjamini–Schramm nonuniqueness conjecture
plain_explanation: On "tree-like" (non-amenable) graphs, there is a range of p where infinitely many infinite clusters coexist (p_c < p_u). This proves the Benjamini–Schramm conjecture.

subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: Canonical O(3) continuum limit and exact O(4) mass asymptotics
plain_explanation: This constructs the continuum limit of the 2D O(3) spin model, a quantum field theory with a mass gap, and finds the exact mass asymptotics for O(4). It is in the spirit of the Yang–Mills mass-gap problem, but in a simpler two-dimensional model.

subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: Critical and near-critical XY scaling and BKT universality
plain_explanation: For the XY model of planar spins and its Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless transition (Nobel Prize 2016), this proves the precise critical correlation decay r^(−1/4)(log r)^(1/8) and the predicted essential singularity of the correlation length.

subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: The low-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick fluctuation law
plain_explanation: For the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick spin glass at low temperature, this proves the free energy fluctuates on the predicted n^(1/6) scale, with a uniquely characterized limiting law.

subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: Conformal universality for weakly interacting and random-bond Ising models
plain_explanation: Universality for the Ising model: small changes to the interactions, or weak random disorder, do not change its critical large-scale picture (spin fields and SLE₃ interfaces).

subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: GOE bulk universality for regular graphs with weak Anderson disorder
plain_explanation: The eigenvalues of a random d-regular graph (every vertex has d neighbours) follow the GOE random-matrix statistics at small scales, even for d = 3 and with weak random disorder added.
quant_note: Random-matrix theory is used to clean correlation matrices: eigenvalues inside the "noise band" are treated as noise. Results like this extend "eigenvalue statistics are universal" to sparse structures. Background only; the standard Marchenko–Pastur cleaning workflow is unchanged.

subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: Directional zero–one laws beyond iid environments and iid ballisticity
plain_explanation: For a random walk in a random environment on ℤ^d, escaping in a given direction has probability 0 or 1, and escaping in a direction forces a positive limiting speed (the ballisticity conjecture).

subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: The Mézard–Parisi formula for diluted spin glasses
plain_explanation: The Mézard–Parisi formula from physics gives the free energy of sparse ("diluted") spin glasses, a class that includes random-satisfiability-type models. This proves it under stated factorization and positivity assumptions.

subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: Perceptron free energies and microscopic jamming exponents
plain_explanation: A perceptron is the simplest neural network: a linear yes/no rule. "How many random patterns can it fit?" is a capacity question. This computes exact free energies for Ising and spherical perceptrons, and the "jamming" exponents at the critical density.
quant_note: This is the capacity (overfitting) question for linear rules. A linear rule with N features can perfectly fit about 2N random ±1 labels (Cover's classic result), so a backtest classifier with too few samples per feature can "explain" pure noise. These papers give exact formulas for richer versions of this. Rule of thumb: keep samples well above 2 × features, and compare the in-sample fit to the fit you get on shuffled labels.

subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: Random-cluster interfaces: critical, disordered, thermal, and natural-time scaling
plain_explanation: Interfaces in the critical random-cluster (FK) model converge to the random fractal curves SLE_κ, and nested loops converge to CLE_κ. This is conformal invariance of critical models for 0 < q ≤ 4.

subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: Critical and quenched near-critical universality for Poisson–Voronoi percolation
plain_explanation: For percolation on random Voronoi cells, this proves Cardy's formula for crossing probabilities and shows near-critical behaviour is universal.

subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: Gaussian free field limits throughout the balanced six-vertex regime
plain_explanation: Height functions of the six-vertex model (a classic ice model) converge to the Gaussian free field throughout the balanced regime, with an exact variance constant 1/arcsin(c/2).

subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: The double-dimer loop ensemble converges to CLE_4
plain_explanation: The loops formed by overlaying two random dimer tilings converge to the conformal loop ensemble CLE₄, the curves themselves and not just statistics about them.

subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: Critical SK autocorrelation processes and dynamics across the temperature transition
plain_explanation: For the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick spin glass under heat-bath dynamics, this proves equilibrium is reached fast at high temperature (cutoff on the log n scale), in about n^(2/3) at the critical point, and only after stretched-exponential time at low temperature. "Critical slowing down" is made rigorous.

subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: Continuum phase transitions for radial pair potentials
plain_explanation: This builds simple distance-based forces between particles in 3D that produce a genuine first-order phase transition (a jump, like boiling), answering Simon's question about continuum phase transitions.

subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: Exact three- and four-state reconstruction thresholds and four-state tree capacity
plain_explanation: Broadcasting on trees: a symbol is passed down a tree with noise at each step; can you guess the root from the leaves? This proves the exact threshold dλ² > 1 for 3- and 4-state models. Consequence: an exact threshold for detecting 3 communities in sparse networks (the stochastic block model).
quant_note: When clustering assets or accounts into 3 groups from a sparse network, below this threshold no method beats random guessing. Check whether your network is above it before trusting cluster labels.
politeia_note: Before showing "there are 3 camps in this discussion network", check the signal is above the detection threshold (a − b)² > 3(a + 2b), where a and b are the within-group and between-group link rates. Below it, any community map is noise.

subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: Exact Hausdorff gauges for SLE
plain_explanation: This finds the exact Hausdorff "gauge" for SLE curves, the precise way to measure the size of these random fractal curves, answering Schramm's question.

subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: The free uniform spanning forest is a factor of IID
plain_explanation: On every graph, the free uniform spanning forest can be produced by a local rule from independent random labels at the vertices (a "factor of IID"); the same holds for a broad class of determinantal processes.

subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: Gaussian fields and interfaces for triangular-lattice Lipschitz heights
plain_explanation: Random Lipschitz height functions on the triangular lattice converge to the Gaussian free field, and their interface converges to SLE₄ at a tuned boundary, confirming Schramm's predictions. Papers were revised on Oct 7.

subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: The joint critical Ashkin–Teller current limit
plain_explanation: This finds the joint scaling limit of heights and current clusters for the critical Ashkin–Teller model along its whole critical line. The paper was revised on Oct 7.

subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: All-temperature pressure of orthogonally invariant Ising spin glasses
plain_explanation: For spin glasses whose coupling matrix is a random rotation of a fixed spectrum, this gives an exact formula for the limiting free energy at every temperature.

subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: Limiting random SAT thresholds, sharp variance and computability
plain_explanation: Random k-SAT: a random logic formula with αn clauses switches sharply from satisfiable to unsatisfiable as α grows. This proves a limiting threshold exists for every k ≥ 3, that the hitting time has variance of order n, and that the 3-SAT threshold is computable. OpenAI credits Gaia Carenini, whose concurrent paper (public Oct 5, 2026) resolved threshold existence first.

subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: The exact factor-of-IID threshold for free Ising spins on trees
plain_explanation: For the Ising model on a regular tree, this finds exactly when the free state can be generated by a local rule from independent randomness: tanh β ≤ 1/√(d − 1).

subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: The three-quarter exponent for honeycomb self-avoiding walk
plain_explanation: A self-avoiding walk never revisits a point. This proves a random n-step self-avoiding walk on the honeycomb lattice spans a distance of about n^(3/4), Nienhuis's 1982 prediction (13 papers).

subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: Optimal logarithmic mixing of the Thorp shuffle
plain_explanation: The Thorp shuffle cuts the deck in half and interleaves the halves, flipping a coin for each pair to decide which card goes first. This proves about log N shuffles randomize N = 2^d cards, the optimal order.
politeia_note: The Thorp shuffle is an engine behind "format-preserving encryption", which scrambles IDs while keeping their format (for example, pseudonymising record numbers). Faster provable mixing means security proofs need fewer rounds. Background only; use a vetted standard (such as NIST FF1) rather than rolling your own.

subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: Sharp singularity rates for symmetric random sign matrices
plain_explanation: A random symmetric matrix of ±1 entries is singular (determinant 0) with probability (1/2 + o(1))ⁿ, the sharp rate, with a matching formula for biased signs.

subject: Mathematical logic
title: Shelah's eventual categoricity and the prescribed-threshold obstruction
plain_explanation: Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture: if a class of mathematical structures has exactly one model (up to isomorphism) at one large size, it has exactly one at every larger size. Proven in ZFC.

subject: Mathematical logic
title: Rigidity of the Turing degrees
plain_explanation: The Turing degrees rank problems by "what can compute what". This proves this ordering has no nontrivial symmetries (it is rigid), a long-open problem in computability theory.

subject: Mathematical logic
title: Single-fold Diophantine representations and undecidability under an at-most-one-solution promise
plain_explanation: Every computably enumerable set has a Diophantine representation with exactly one solution per member (single-fold). So Hilbert's 10th problem stays undecidable even under an "at most one solution" promise.

subject: Mathematical logic
title: Separating choiceless counting from polynomial time and witnessed choice
plain_explanation: Choiceless polynomial time with counting, a leading candidate logic for capturing polynomial time, cannot express whether a linear system over 𝔽₃ is solvable. This confirms the Blass–Gurevich–Shelah non-capture conjecture.

subject: Mathematical logic
title: The Partition Principle does not imply Choice
plain_explanation: Without the axiom of choice, does the Partition Principle (if A maps onto B, then B fits inside A) imply full Choice? This is one of the oldest open problems in set theory. This shows it does not.

subject: Mathematical logic
title: Weak normalization implies strong normalization in pure type systems
plain_explanation: In pure type systems (the logical foundation of proof assistants), if every term can be simplified to a normal form, then every simplification process terminates (weak implies strong normalization). The Barendregt–Geuvers–Klop conjecture.

subject: Group theory
title: Cannon's conjecture
plain_explanation: Cannon's conjecture: any hyperbolic group whose boundary is a 2-sphere is essentially the fundamental group of a hyperbolic 3-manifold. One of the central problems of geometric group theory. Proven.

subject: Group theory
title: An infinite finitely presented residually finite 2-group and a finitely presented nil algebra
plain_explanation: This builds an infinite, finitely presented group in which every element has finite order that is a power of 2, a negative answer to the finitely presented Burnside problem, plus a finitely presented nil algebra.

subject: Group theory
title: Thompson's group F is nonamenable
plain_explanation: Thompson's group F (piecewise-linear maps of an interval with dyadic breakpoints) is proven non-amenable. This is a famous problem with a long history of claimed solutions.

subject: Group theory
title: A finitely generated Eilenberg–Ganea counterexample
plain_explanation: The Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture is disproved by a finitely generated group of cohomological dimension 2 but geometric dimension 3.

subject: Group theory
title: Boone–Higman embeddings with higher finiteness
plain_explanation: Boone–Higman conjecture: a finitely generated group has a solvable word problem exactly when it sits inside a finitely presented simple group. Proven, with strong finiteness.

subject: Group theory
title: Amenability, unitarizability, and strong Ulam stability
plain_explanation: Dixmier's problem: a group is amenable exactly when all its uniformly bounded representations can be made unitary. Proven for all discrete groups, along with a characterization by Ulam stability.

subject: Group theory
title: A torsion-free hyperbolic group that is neither residually finite nor linear over any field
plain_explanation: This builds a torsion-free hyperbolic group that is not residually finite and not linear over any field, answering a famous question about hyperbolic groups negatively.

subject: Group theory
title: An infinite finitely presented simple amenable group
plain_explanation: This builds an infinite, finitely presented, simple, amenable group, showing these properties can all occur together.

subject: Group theory
title: Classifying spaces and geometric obstructions for Artin groups
plain_explanation: The Artin K(π,1) conjecture is proven for all finite-rank Artin groups, along with the parabolic intersection conjecture, and an Artin group is found with no geometric CAT(0) action.

subject: Group theory
title: Quasi-isometric recognition of virtually polycyclic groups
plain_explanation: Any group that looks like a virtually polycyclic group from far away (quasi-isometric) is itself virtually polycyclic. The Eskin–Fisher–Whyte conjecture.

subject: Group theory
title: Nonsingular systems of equations over arbitrary groups
plain_explanation: Kervaire's conjecture: adding one new generator and one new relation to a nontrivial group can never make it trivial. Proven, together with Howie's conjecture on solving equations over groups.

subject: Group theory
title: A hyperbolic group without a geometric CAT(0) action
plain_explanation: This gives a hyperbolic group with no proper cocompact action on any CAT(0) space, answering the "are all hyperbolic groups CAT(0)?" question negatively.

subject: Group theory
title: Gersten’s conjecture and virtual compact specialness of one-relator groups
plain_explanation: Gersten's conjecture: one-relator groups with no Baumslag–Solitar subgroups are hyperbolic. Proven, along with "virtual compact specialness" for hyperbolic one-relator groups.

subject: Group theory
title: A group without fixed price
plain_explanation: Gaboriau's fixed-price problem: this builds a group with two free measure-preserving actions of different "cost", answering it negatively.

subject: Mathematical physics
title: Spacetime Penrose inequalities: enclosing area, charge, rotation, and anti-de Sitter extensions
plain_explanation: The Penrose inequality from General Relativity says a spacetime's total mass is at least what the area of its black holes requires. This proves the full spacetime version (not only the time-symmetric case) in all dimensions, with charged, rotating (Kerr–Newman) and anti-de Sitter variants (13 papers).

subject: Mathematical physics
title: Localization and delocalization in the Anderson model
plain_explanation: Anderson localization concerns electrons in a disordered crystal. This proves that in 2D any amount of disorder traps them, while in 3D and above weak disorder still lets them travel (absolutely continuous spectrum), the long-sought "extended states" result.

subject: Mathematical physics
title: Sharp finite-matrix Lieb–Thirring inequalities and all equality cases
plain_explanation: This proves the sharp Lieb–Thirring inequality in one dimension for matrix-valued potentials, with all equality cases (sums of solitons).

subject: Mathematical physics
title: The ionization and generalized ionization conjectures
plain_explanation: The ionization conjecture: a molecule with nuclear charge Z and M nuclei can bind at most Z + C·M electrons, and atomic ionization energies and radii have universal bounds. Proven.

subject: Mathematical physics
title: Strong cosmic censorship near two-ended Kerr data
plain_explanation: Strong cosmic censorship near rotating Kerr black holes: for generic perturbations, spacetime cannot be continued past the inner horizon in a reasonable sense, so General Relativity stays deterministic.

subject: Mathematical physics
title: Area laws and tensor networks for two-dimensional gapped systems
plain_explanation: The area law: ground states of gapped 2D quantum systems have entanglement proportional to boundary length, and can be approximated by PEPS tensor networks of polynomial size.

subject: Mathematical physics
title: Exactly three mutually unbiased bases in dimension six
plain_explanation: In quantum information, mutually unbiased bases are measurement settings that are "maximally different". This proves dimension 6 has exactly 3 of them, not 4, using a certified computer computation.

subject: Mathematical physics
title: Positive-temperature Bose–Einstein condensation and exact quantum depletion
plain_explanation: This proves Bose–Einstein condensation for a gas of hard spheres at positive temperature, a central open problem in mathematical physics, plus Bogoliubov's quantum-depletion law at zero temperature.

subject: Mathematical physics
title: The spin-one Haldane gap
plain_explanation: The Haldane gap: a chain of spin-1 particles with antiferromagnetic Heisenberg interactions has an energy gap, as Haldane predicted in 1983 (Nobel Prize 2016). Proven.

subject: Mathematical physics
title: Uniform Laughlin gap and stability under bounded scalar disorder
plain_explanation: For the Laughlin state of the fractional quantum Hall effect (filling 1/3), this proves a uniform energy gap that survives weak disorder.

subject: Mathematical physics
title: Threshold and positive-energy bound states of the BFSS matrix model
plain_explanation: The BFSS matrix model is a proposed definition of M-theory. This proves it has exactly one zero-energy bound state for every SU(N), while for SU(2) it has infinitely many positive-energy bound states, contradicting the original paper.

subject: Mathematical physics
title: Bloch's law, its lattice correction, and the spherical magnetization law
plain_explanation: For the quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet, this proves Bloch's T^(3/2) law with its exact coefficient and lattice correction, and spontaneous magnetization in dimension 3 and above, a famous open problem.

subject: Mathematical physics
title: Entanglement without distillable secret key
plain_explanation: This builds an entangled quantum state from which no secret key can be distilled (for the stated protocols), and disproves Christandl's PPT-square conjecture.

subject: Mathematical physics
title: The entropy photon-number inequality
plain_explanation: The entropy photon-number inequality, the quantum-optics analogue of Shannon's entropy power inequality, is proven for beam-splitter mixing.

subject: Mathematical physics
title: Parity is not in QAC^0
plain_explanation: Moore's conjecture: constant-depth quantum circuits (QAC⁰) cannot compute parity, even with large Toffoli gates. Proven.

subject: Mathematical physics
title: QMA-hardness of continuum Coulomb energy
plain_explanation: Computing the ground-state energy of electrons in a molecule (the full continuum Coulomb model) is QMA-hard: hard even for quantum computers in the worst case.

subject: Mathematical physics
title: Classical capacity of generalized amplitude damping
plain_explanation: This computes the exact classical capacity of the generalized amplitude-damping quantum channel (how many bits per use it can carry).

subject: Mathematical physics
title: Threshold repetition for entangled games
plain_explanation: For two-player games where players share entanglement, the chance of winning noticeably more than a v fraction of k repetitions decays exponentially in k (threshold parallel repetition).

subject: Mathematical physics
title: Failure of Kohn–Sham ensemble representation
plain_explanation: Kohn–Sham ensemble representability, a foundation of density functional theory in chemistry, fails: this gives a 3-electron molecule whose ground-state density has no non-interacting representation.

subject: Mathematical physics
title: Exact quantum factoring over a fixed finite gate set
plain_explanation: This gives a polynomial-size quantum circuit family, using one fixed finite gate set, that outputs the complete prime factorization of any integer with probability exactly 1.
quant_note: For BTC holders: this is not a new threat. It is about factoring (RSA), not the elliptic-curve signatures Bitcoin uses, and Shor's algorithm already broke both in theory on a large enough quantum computer. The practical risk timeline still depends on quantum hardware.
politeia_note: The same holds for e-voting or identity cryptography: no new practical threat. Plan the move to post-quantum cryptography on the normal timeline.

subject: Mathematical physics
title: Unitary vertex operator algebras and conformal nets
plain_explanation: Two mathematical frameworks for 2D conformal field theory (vertex operator algebras and conformal nets) agree for strongly rational unitary theories.

subject: Mathematical physics
title: QAOA attains the SK optimum in the thermodynamic-first limit
plain_explanation: QAOA, a quantum optimization algorithm, reaches the optimal energy of the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick spin glass when system size grows before circuit depth, with consequences for MaxCut on random graphs.
quant_note: Quantum portfolio optimization is heavily marketed. This proves QAOA can match the optimum of a model spin-glass problem in one specific limit; it says nothing about beating classical solvers on real portfolio problems.

subject: Mathematical physics
title: From scale symmetry to local conformal symmetry in four-dimensional QFT
plain_explanation: Under stated hypotheses, scale symmetry implies local conformal symmetry for 4D quantum field theories, a long-standing physics expectation.

subject: Mathematical physics
title: Polynomial-time unitary synthesis from a Boolean oracle
plain_explanation: The Aaronson–Kuperberg unitary synthesis problem: any n-qubit unitary can be approximated by a polynomial-size quantum circuit that queries a suitably chosen Boolean oracle.

subject: Mathematical physics
title: The optimal quartic separation between randomized and quantum queries
plain_explanation: The gap between randomized and quantum query complexity for total functions can be quartic: R(f) = O(Q(f)⁴) is tight in its exponent, disproving the conjectured cubic relation.

subject: Operator algebras
title: Counterexamples to Baum–Connes and Kadison–Kaplansky
plain_explanation: The Baum–Connes conjecture links the topology of a group to its operator algebra. This disproves its coefficient-free reduced form (both injectivity and surjectivity fail), and disproves the Kadison–Kaplansky conjecture with a torsion-free group whose reduced C*-algebra has a nontrivial projection.

subject: Operator algebras
title: Rigidity and arithmetic of lattice von Neumann algebras
plain_explanation: For von Neumann algebras built from lattices in Lie groups over local fields, this classifies all finite-index "bridges" (bimodules) between them, and recovers the original group from the algebra (a strong rigidity theorem).

subject: Operator algebras
title: Isomorphism of the free group factors
plain_explanation: The free group factor problem asks whether the von Neumann algebras of the free groups on 2 and on 3 generators are the same. It is one of the most famous open problems in operator algebras. This proves they are isomorphic, so all free group factors coincide.

subject: Operator algebras
title: Kadison's similarity conjecture
plain_explanation: Kadison's similarity problem (1955): every bounded representation of a C*-algebra on Hilbert space becomes a *-representation after a change of coordinates. Proven.

subject: Operator algebras
title: Strong Kadison–Kastler stability and its spatial boundaries
plain_explanation: Two von Neumann algebras that are close enough are conjugate by a unitary close to the identity (strong Kadison–Kastler stability). Counterexamples show where this stops working.

subject: Operator algebras
title: Relative bicentralizers and modular spectral recovery
plain_explanation: This proves Connes' bicentralizer conjecture for every type III₁ factor, and a relative version for inclusions.

subject: Operator algebras
title: Cuntz comparison, nuclear dimension, and equivariant Jiang–Su stability
plain_explanation: This proves the unital Toms–Winter conjecture (three regularity properties of simple nuclear C*-algebras are equivalent) and equivariant Jiang–Su stability for amenable group actions (Szabó's conjecture, in this case).

subject: Operator algebras
title: Kirchberg's O_2 norm-ultrapower embedding problem
plain_explanation: Kirchberg's question about embedding into ultrapowers of the Cuntz algebra O₂ is answered negatively with an explicit group C*-algebra.

subject: Operator algebras
title: Invariant projections, hyperinvariant subspaces, and transitive algebras
plain_explanation: This builds a quasinilpotent operator on Hilbert space with no nontrivial subspace left invariant by everything that commutes with it. That answers the hyperinvariant subspace question, a close relative of the famous invariant subspace problem.

subject: Operator algebras
title: Kaplansky's quasitrace conjecture and failure of tensor-product stable finiteness
plain_explanation: Kaplansky's quasitrace conjecture is disproved, and as a consequence the tensor product of two stably finite simple C*-algebras can be properly infinite.

subject: Operator algebras
title: The Kadison–Ringrose cohomology conjecture
plain_explanation: The Kadison–Ringrose conjecture: all higher bounded Hochschild cohomology of a von Neumann algebra (with coefficients in itself) vanishes. Proven.

subject: Operator algebras
title: The generator problem for finite factors
plain_explanation: The generator problem: every II₁ factor with separable predual is generated by a single operator. A famous open problem. Proven.

subject: Operator algebras
title: A ZFC counterexample to Naimark's problem
plain_explanation: Naimark's problem: this gives an alternative ZFC construction (after Tanaka's earlier one) of an infinite-dimensional simple C*-algebra with only one irreducible representation.

subject: Operator algebras
title: Two notions of free entropy differ even when both are finite
plain_explanation: Voiculescu defined "free entropy" in two ways, via matrix approximations and via free Fisher information. This shows they can differ even when both are finite.

subject: Operator algebras
title: The Kirchberg–Rørdam character criterion and infinite tensor-power Jiang–Su stability
plain_explanation: A C*-algebra is Jiang–Su stable exactly when its central-sequence algebra has no characters. This answers Kirchberg–Rørdam, and also the Dadarlat–Toms question about infinite tensor powers.

subject: Operator algebras
title: Approximation and quadratic strong-operator paving
plain_explanation: This proves the Popa–Vaes quadratic paving conjecture: self-adjoint operators can be "paved" into O(ε^−2) nearly diagonal blocks relative to any maximal abelian subalgebra.

subject: Operator algebras
title: Trace cones and Razak–Jacelon stabilization
plain_explanation: This classifies separable nuclear C*-algebras after stabilizing with the Razak–Jacelon algebra, using their cones of traces, which answers Robert's question.

subject: Operator algebras
title: Radius of comparison equals half the mean dimension
plain_explanation: For minimal dynamical systems, the radius of comparison of the crossed-product C*-algebra equals half the mean dimension of the system, a conjectured bridge between dynamics and operator algebras.

subject: Operator algebras
title: Weak pure infiniteness and Cuntz-algebra absorption
plain_explanation: Weak pure infiniteness implies absorption of the Cuntz algebra O∞ for separable nuclear algebras, resolving a Kirchberg–Rørdam question.

subject: Topology
title: The Hilbert–Smith conjecture in every dimension
plain_explanation: The Hilbert–Smith conjecture: any locally compact group acting faithfully and continuously on a finite-dimensional manifold must be a Lie group. This is the last piece of Hilbert's 5th problem. Proven in every dimension.

subject: Topology
title: Four-dimensional disk embedding and Wall's conjecture
plain_explanation: In 4-dimensional topology, the unrestricted disk-embedding conjecture fails (the free group F₂ is not "good" in Freedman–Quinn's sense). Wall's conjecture is also disproved: some 4-dimensional Poincaré-duality group is not the fundamental group of any aspherical 4-manifold.

subject: Topology
title: The purely cosmetic surgery conjecture
plain_explanation: The purely cosmetic surgery conjecture: doing two different Dehn surgeries on a nontrivial knot never produces the same oriented 3-manifold. Proven.

subject: Topology
title: Failure of rational injectivity for maximal coarse assembly
plain_explanation: The rational coarse Novikov conjecture is disproved: this builds a bounded-geometry space whose coarse assembly map is not rationally injective.

subject: Topology
title: Finite Smith–Toda complexes at every height
plain_explanation: Smith–Toda complexes V(n), building blocks of chromatic homotopy theory, exist at every height if the prime is allowed to vary. For example, V(4) exists at p = 1009.

subject: Topology
title: The Kervaire invariant problem at the prime three
plain_explanation: This resolves the Kervaire invariant problem at the prime 3: exactly the classes in stems 10, 106 and 322 survive.

subject: Topology
title: Quillen's conjecture in rational homology
plain_explanation: Quillen's conjecture (rational homology form): for a finite group with no nontrivial normal p-subgroup, the poset of elementary abelian p-subgroups is not contractible. Proven for every group and prime.

subject: Topology
title: The Hovey–Strickland and Chai conjectures
plain_explanation: This proves Chai's conjecture and, through it, the Hovey–Strickland conjecture classifying the thick tensor ideals of dualizable K(n)-local spectra.

subject: Topology
title: The Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis
plain_explanation: Grothendieck's homotopy hypothesis: his algebraic ∞-groupoids (with the Ara–Henry conventions) recover exactly the homotopy theory of spaces. Proven.

subject: Topology
title: Finite generation for the K(n)-local sphere
plain_explanation: Every homotopy group of the K(n)-local sphere is finitely generated, answering Hovey and Strickland.

subject: Topology
title: Cyclic length and chromatic fixed-point loss
plain_explanation: This determines exactly how much "chromatic height" is lost when passing between fixed points of a p-group and of a subgroup: it equals the length of the shortest cyclic subnormal chain.

subject: Topology
title: The four-dimensional Singer conjecture
plain_explanation: The Singer conjecture in dimension 4: the L²-Betti numbers of aspherical 4-manifolds vanish outside the middle degree. Proven.

subject: Topology
title: Curtis’s conjecture
plain_explanation: Curtis's conjecture: at the prime 2, the only stable homotopy classes of spheres detected by homology are the Hopf-invariant-one and Kervaire-invariant-one classes. Proven.

subject: Topology
title: Thomason model structures in all strict higher dimensions
plain_explanation: The Ara–Maltsiniotis conjecture: strict n-categories (in every dimension, including ω) model the homotopy theory of spaces via Thomason model structures. Proven.

subject: Topology
title: Chromatic splitting: filtrations and counterexamples
plain_explanation: The chromatic splitting conjecture is disproved at height 3 for primes p ≥ 5 (and weak splitting in other cases), while a corrected filtration by the predicted pieces is proven.

subject: Topology
title: Counterexamples to finite generation at chromatic height two
plain_explanation: The Hahn–Wilson conjecture is refuted at chromatic height 2 by spectra that cannot be built from BP⟨2⟩ in finitely many steps.

subject: Topology
title: Nonhomeomorphic closed aspherical four-manifolds
plain_explanation: The Borel conjecture says aspherical manifolds with the same homotopy type are homeomorphic. This disproves it in dimension 4 with homotopy-equivalent but non-homeomorphic aspherical 4-manifolds.

subject: Topology
title: A counterexample to Wall's finite D(2) problem
plain_explanation: Wall's D(2) problem is answered with a counterexample: a 3-dimensional complex that looks 2-dimensional to every homological test but has no 2-dimensional model.

subject: Functional analysis
title: Tingley’s sphere-isometry problem
plain_explanation: Tingley's problem: any distance-preserving map between the unit spheres of two Banach spaces extends to a linear isometry of the whole spaces. Proven in full generality.

subject: Functional analysis
title: Independence of the separable quotient problem
plain_explanation: The separable quotient problem (does every infinite-dimensional Banach space have a separable infinite-dimensional quotient?) is independent of the usual axioms ZFC, relative to a measurable cardinal.

subject: Functional analysis
title: Lipschitz equivalent Banach spaces need not be linearly isomorphic
plain_explanation: Two separable Banach spaces can be equivalent as metric spaces (bi-Lipschitz) without being linearly isomorphic, resolving a major open problem negatively.

subject: Functional analysis
title: The complete Crouzeix conjecture
plain_explanation: The complete Crouzeix conjecture: for any matrix or operator A and any (matrix) polynomial p, ‖p(A)‖ is at most 2 × the largest value of |p| on the numerical range of A. The constant 2 is sharp. This also settles the famous scalar Crouzeix conjecture.

subject: Functional analysis
title: The cotype–cotype conjecture under the approximation property
plain_explanation: The cotype–cotype conjecture (for spaces with the approximation property): a Banach space is K-convex exactly when it and its dual both have finite cotype. Proven.

subject: Functional analysis
title: Markov type characterizes superreflexivity
plain_explanation: Nontrivial Markov type characterizes superreflexive Banach spaces, answering Naor's renorming question.

subject: Functional analysis
title: Nonexpansive fixed points in reflexive Banach spaces
plain_explanation: Kirk's fixed-point problem: every distance-non-increasing self-map of a closed, bounded, convex set in a reflexive Banach space has a fixed point. Proven.

subject: Functional analysis
title: A counterexample to metric-entropy duality
plain_explanation: Pietsch's duality conjecture for metric entropy (covering numbers of a convex body versus those of its polar) is disproved.

subject: Functional analysis
title: A uniformly discrete counterexample to bounded approximation in Lipschitz-free spaces
plain_explanation: This answers Kalton's question with a countable uniformly discrete metric space whose Lipschitz-free space has the approximation property but not the bounded approximation property.

subject: Functional analysis
title: Reflexive midpoint convexity and diamond distortion
plain_explanation: This builds a reflexive Banach space with asymptotic midpoint uniform convexity but no asymptotically uniformly convex renorming, and with unbounded distortion for branching diamond graphs.

subject: Functional analysis
title: Metric Markov cotype of ℓ_1 and Hilbert-space Lipschitz extension
plain_explanation: The space ℓ₁ has metric Markov cotype 2, so Lipschitz maps from subsets of Hilbert space into ℓ₁ extend to the whole space with bounded loss (Ball's extension problem for this target).

subject: Differential geometry
title: Smooth isometric immersions of surfaces into ℝ^4
plain_explanation: Every closed surface, with any way of measuring lengths on it, can be placed smoothly into 4-dimensional space without stretching (a smooth isometric immersion into ℝ⁴).

subject: Differential geometry
title: A smooth surface metric with no local isometric immersion in ℝ^3
plain_explanation: This builds a smooth way of measuring lengths on a small patch of surface that cannot be realized as an actual surface in 3D space, even after shrinking the patch. A classical question answered negatively.

subject: Differential geometry
title: Gromov’s integral scalar-curvature bound for simplicial volume
plain_explanation: This proves Gromov's integral bound linking negative scalar curvature to simplicial volume, and the Gromov–Lawson conjecture: closed aspherical manifolds cannot carry positive scalar curvature, and any nonnegative-scalar-curvature metric on one is flat.

subject: Differential geometry
title: Spectral scalar curvature, Urysohn width, and macroscopic dimension
plain_explanation: Manifolds with positive "spectral" scalar curvature are thin in all but n − 2 directions (bounded Urysohn width), strengthening Gromov's width theorem.

subject: Differential geometry
title: Sharp Cartan–Hadamard isoperimetry and rigidity
plain_explanation: The Cartan–Hadamard conjecture: in nonpositively curved spaces, balls enclose at least as much volume for a given surface area as in flat space (the isoperimetric inequality). Proven in all dimensions, with sharp filling bounds in CAT(0) spaces.

subject: Differential geometry
title: Yau's uniformization conjecture
plain_explanation: Yau's uniformization conjecture: a complete non-compact Kähler manifold with positive bisectional curvature is biholomorphic to ℂⁿ. Proven.

subject: Differential geometry
title: Katok's entropy rigidity conjecture
plain_explanation: Katok's entropy rigidity conjecture: on a negatively curved manifold, the natural (Liouville) measure has maximal entropy only when the metric is locally symmetric. Proven in dimension 3 and up.

subject: Differential geometry
title: A counterexample to the nearby Lagrangian conjecture
plain_explanation: The nearby Lagrangian conjecture is disproved: in a high-dimensional cotangent bundle there is a closed exact Lagrangian that is not Hamiltonian-isotopic to the zero section.

subject: Differential geometry
title: Donaldson's hypersymplectic deformation conjecture
plain_explanation: Donaldson's hypersymplectic deformation conjecture: positive triples of closed 2-forms on a 4-manifold deform to hyperkähler triples while keeping their cohomology. Proven. The paper was revised on Oct 7.

subject: Differential geometry
title: Donaldson's tamed-to-compatible conjecture
plain_explanation: Donaldson's tamed-to-compatible conjecture: on a closed 4-manifold, an almost complex structure tamed by some symplectic form is compatible with some (possibly different) symplectic form. Proven; revised on Oct 7 to correct a side claim.

subject: Differential geometry
title: Symplectic ball packing in higher dimensions
plain_explanation: Symplectic ball packing: this gives the exact rule for when several symplectic balls fit disjointly inside a bigger one in dimension 6 and higher (the Siegel–Yao conjecture).

subject: Differential geometry
title: The metric Blaschke conjecture
plain_explanation: The metric Blaschke conjecture: a manifold whose injectivity radius equals its diameter is, up to scaling, a round sphere or projective space. Proven.

subject: Differential geometry
title: Infinitely many closed geodesics on Riemannian spheres and closed three-manifolds
plain_explanation: Every way of measuring lengths on a sphere of any dimension has infinitely many different closed geodesics (closed "straightest" loops). The same holds on every closed 3-manifold.

subject: Differential geometry
title: Sharp singular-set bounds for stationary integral varifolds
plain_explanation: Stationary integral varifolds are a very general notion of minimal surface, such as soap films. This proves their singular set has dimension at most m − 1, which is sharp, and almost-everywhere regularity on round spheres.

subject: Differential geometry
title: Counterexamples to stable-Morse and strong Arnold fixed-point bounds
plain_explanation: Lower bounds in the spirit of the Arnold conjecture fail: on certain 22-dimensional manifolds, Hamiltonian maps can have far fewer fixed points than the stable Morse number, and one map of the quadric threefold has only 3 fixed points.

subject: Differential geometry
title: Nonnegative-curvature Einstein classification and an L^2 topological gap
plain_explanation: This classifies Einstein 4-manifolds with positive Einstein constant and nonnegative curvature (only the round sphere, ℂP² and S² × S²), and proves an L² gap theorem.

subject: Differential geometry
title: The Solomon–Yau least-volume conjecture
plain_explanation: The Solomon–Yau conjecture: the least-volume non-trivial minimal hypersurface in a round sphere is the smallest Clifford product. Proven.

subject: Differential geometry
title: Yau’s nodal bounds: surfaces and higher dimensions
plain_explanation: Yau's nodal conjecture asks how long the zero lines of vibration modes (eigenfunctions) can be. On surfaces, this proves the sharp bound C·√λ. It also shows the bound fails in dimensions 3, 4 and 5.

subject: Differential geometry
title: Scalar curvature and finite-time Ricci-flow singularities
plain_explanation: In 4D, Ricci flow can be continued as long as scalar curvature stays bounded. In higher dimensions this fails, shown by a counterexample.

subject: Differential geometry
title: A finite-time singularity of Calabi flow
plain_explanation: Calabi flow can form a singularity in finite time (shown on ℂP¹⁰), disproving Chen's long-time existence conjecture.

subject: Differential geometry
title: Affine Bernstein rigidity through dimension nine and a smooth dimension-ten counterexample
plain_explanation: The affine Bernstein problem: complete affine-maximal graphs are paraboloids in dimensions 3 through 9, and a smooth counterexample exists in dimension 10, so the range is sharp.

subject: Differential geometry
title: The isoperimetric profile of the cubic three-torus
plain_explanation: This finds the least-area way to enclose each volume inside a cubic 3-torus, and classifies all minimizers: balls, tubes, slabs, and their complements.

subject: Differential geometry
title: Unique tangent flows at the first surface singularity
plain_explanation: For mean curvature flow of surfaces in ℝ³, the zoomed-in picture ("tangent flow") at the first singularity is unique, with no extra assumptions.

subject: Differential geometry
title: Gigli’s characterization of Alexandrov curvature
plain_explanation: Gigli's conjecture: Alexandrov curvature bounds are characterized by the RCD condition with distributional sectional curvature bounds, in every dimension. Proven.

subject: Differential geometry
title: Bi-Lipschitz coordinates at every regular RCD point
plain_explanation: At every regular point of a non-collapsed RCD space (a very general curved space), there are bi-Lipschitz coordinates to ordinary ℝⁿ.

subject: Differential geometry
title: A three-manifold without conjugate points or nonpositive curvature
plain_explanation: This gives a closed 3-manifold that admits a metric without conjugate points but no metric of nonpositive curvature, answering an old question negatively.

subject: Differential geometry
title: Negative Kähler curvature without bounded holomorphic coordinates
plain_explanation: This builds a domain in ℂ³ with a complete, negatively pinched Kähler metric but no bounded holomorphic coordinates, disproving bounded-domain uniformization in that setting.

subject: Differential geometry
title: Weak MTW curvature gives convexity and regular optimal transport
plain_explanation: For optimal transport on curved spaces satisfying the weak Ma–Trudinger–Wang condition, this proves Villani's convexity conjecture, and that optimal transport maps are Hölder continuous.

subject: Differential geometry
title: Failure of integer-degree harmonic dimension comparison
plain_explanation: Yau proposed that harmonic functions of polynomial growth on spaces with nonnegative Ricci curvature are no more numerous than in flat space. This disproves the integer-degree version on ℝ³.

subject: Partial differential equations
title: Global smoothness for relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell
plain_explanation: The relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell system describes a plasma: charged particles moving in their own electromagnetic field. This proves smooth solutions exist for all time in 3D for large data, a famous open problem (Glassey–Strauss).

subject: Partial differential equations
title: Nonuniqueness with local conservation for the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation
plain_explanation: For the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation (the basic model of a dilute gas), this builds two different global entropy solutions from the same initial state, so uniqueness fails in this class.

subject: Partial differential equations
title: Kinetic limits and fluctuations over the Boltzmann lifespan
plain_explanation: This derives Boltzmann's gas equation from Newton's laws for many particles over the whole regular time interval (not just a short time), plus the Gaussian fluctuations around it.

subject: Partial differential equations
title: Joint metric and connection recovery from one boundary patch
plain_explanation: In Calderón's inverse problem (the maths of electrical impedance tomography: seeing inside a body from boundary measurements), measurements on one small patch determine a metric and connection in dimension 3 and up. But rough conductivities in 3D cannot always be recovered.

subject: Partial differential equations
title: The planar Mumford–Shah regularity conjecture and local weak-L^4 gradient bounds
plain_explanation: The Mumford–Shah model segments an image into smooth regions separated by edges. This proves the planar regularity conjecture: the edge set of an optimal segmentation is locally a smooth curve, a crack tip, or three curves meeting at 120°.
quant_note: In one dimension the Mumford–Shah energy means "fit a smooth curve, paying a penalty for each jump": a principled regime-change detector. The new result is about 2D image edges, so it is background, but it confirms the model behaves well.

subject: Partial differential equations
title: The critical dimension for the one-phase Bernoulli problem
plain_explanation: For the one-phase Bernoulli free-boundary problem, minimizers are smooth up to dimension 6, and the first singular minimizer appears in dimension 7. This pins down the critical dimension.

subject: Partial differential equations
title: The three-dimensional Ball–Evans approximation problem
plain_explanation: The Ball–Evans approximation problem from elasticity: in 3D, every Sobolev homeomorphism can be approximated by smooth diffeomorphisms. Proven.

subject: Partial differential equations
title: The hot spots conjecture for simply connected planar domains
plain_explanation: The hot spots conjecture (Rauch, 1974): in an insulated, simply connected flat room, the hottest and coldest points of the slowest-decaying temperature pattern are on the walls. Proven in a strict form for smooth simply connected planar domains.

subject: Partial differential equations
title: The Lane–Emden and Hénon–Lane–Emden conjectures
plain_explanation: The Lane–Emden conjecture: in the subcritical range, a classic system of nonlinear elliptic equations has no positive solution on all of space. Proven, with its weighted Hénon extension.

subject: Partial differential equations
title: Stable blowup for the defocusing Schrödinger equation
plain_explanation: The defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation is usually expected to be well behaved. This shows that on a 12-dimensional torus, with a large enough power, finite-time blowup can happen and is stable under small perturbations.

subject: Partial differential equations
title: Global uniqueness in smooth isotropic elasticity
plain_explanation: In 3D elasticity, boundary measurements of displacement and force determine both elastic (Lamé) parameters everywhere inside, without extra assumptions.

subject: Partial differential equations
title: Nonattainment of the three-marginal Coulomb Monge problem
plain_explanation: In multi-marginal Coulomb optimal transport (used in density functional theory), the optimal arrangement of 3 electrons need not be a deterministic function of the first one's position: the "Monge ansatz" fails.

subject: Partial differential equations
title: Sharp one-third stability of Brenier maps
plain_explanation: Optimal transport (Brenier) maps move one probability distribution onto another as cheaply as possible. This proves they are only cube-root stable: if the target moves by δ (in Wasserstein distance), the map can move by about δ^(1/3), and that is sharp. It disproves the conjectured square-root bound.
quant_note: If you use optimal-transport maps to morph one return distribution into another (quantile mapping across regimes, synthetic-scenario generators, distribution-shift correction), the map can be far more sensitive than the distributions: a small change in the target can move the map by its cube root. Test any OT-based scenario generator by perturbing its inputs and measuring how far the mapped scenarios move.

subject: Partial differential equations
title: De Giorgi's conjecture in dimension eight
plain_explanation: De Giorgi's conjecture (1978) at the sharp dimension 8: a solution of the Allen–Cahn phase-transition equation that increases in one direction is really one-dimensional, a flat transition. Proven.

subject: Partial differential equations
title: Universal computation in forced Navier–Stokes flows
plain_explanation: This designs external forces on a viscous 3D fluid so that it simulates any computer program: a marked particle reaches a target region exactly when the program halts. So predicting forced Navier–Stokes flows is undecidable in general. A paper was revised on Oct 7.

subject: Partial differential equations
title: Interior C^{1,\alpha} regularity for infinity-harmonic functions
plain_explanation: Infinity-harmonic functions (the "tug-of-war game" equation, and best Lipschitz extensions) are proven to have Hölder-continuous gradients in every dimension. Before, this was known only in 2D.
